About Base
Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role
Base designs its own hardware, builds it in its own factory, installs it at homes, and sells the power. That vertical integration is our advantage, and it means the suppliers we choose and the deals we strike directly shape our cost and speed.
As a GSM Intern, you will own sourcing for a set of assigned parts, run the RFQ process end to end, and negotiate cost and terms directly with suppliers.
This is not a shadowing internship. You will be given parts to source, suppliers to negotiate with, and quotes that carry real weight in our build cost. The work sits between Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, and Finance, and suits someone who thinks in systems, is comfortable acting on incomplete information, and likes building durable, repeatable sourcing processes.

What You’ll Do
• Own sourcing for a set of assigned parts: build and run RFQs, compare supplier quotes on cost, lead time, and capacity, and make the call on award.

• Negotiate price, payment terms, and lead time directly with suppliers, and track savings against the prior baseline.

• Build supplier cost models — bottoms-up where you can — so you can tell a fair quote from a padded one.

• Support qualification of new suppliers and second sources for critical components: gather quotes, samples, and capability data for the team’s decision.

• Track supplier performance — cost, delivery, and quality — and flag risk before it hits the production line.

What You’ll Bring
• Working toward a degree in supply chain, industrial engineering, operations, mechanical engineering, business, or another quantitative field — or on a comparable path.

• Strong spreadsheet skills and comfort working with large, messy datasets. SQL, Python, or scripting is a plus.

• Genuine interest in how physical products get built. Exposure to an MRP or ERP system (Odoo, SAP, NetSuite) is a plus, not a requirement.

• Clear, direct written communication — you will send RFQs, quote comparisons, and escalations to suppliers and internal teams.

• Bias to action and follow-through. You close loops without being asked twice.

• Available to work in person in Austin, TX for the duration of the internship.

About the Team
Global Supply Management owns every part that goes into a Base battery and its associated systems. This includes sourcing, planning, and getting it to the line on time. We are ramping in-house manufacturing of our own battery product while qualifying second sources for critical components, which means the plan changes often and the cost of being wrong is a stopped line. Sourcing is where that pressure land

The Non-Destructive Evaluation and Damage Tolerance Group serving the Non-Destructive Evaluation and Damage Tolerance Branch (EM21) at Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) in Huntsville, AL has an opening for a Damage Tolerance Intern (DT). The Damage Tolerance Team is responsible for performing analysis of structures and materials as related to lifespan, fracture, fatigue, and damage tolerance. These analyses are critical to failure evaluation and fitness for service criteria for spaceflight and ground based systems at NASA. There are many different aspects to a full damage tolerance assessment, each one a critical part of the integrity of the target article. Evaluations are performed by material test evaluation, FEA modeling, stress analysis and NASGRO models, combined into a safe life assessment. In this position, an intern would be: learning the basic fundamentals of fatigue and fracture mechanics; utilizing ASTM standards to evaluate data sets for valuable material information; creating programs to assist with evaluation of large data sets; collecting data on various material properties to further expand the characterization of certain materials; running analysis on various crack cases to determine critical crack sizes and life expectancies. These tasks will give the intern an opportunity to experience the full range of opportunities found in the damage tolerance branch. Be a part of our team, as we support the exciting challenge to return mankind back to the Moon and beyond.

The Damage Tolerance Intern will:
• Problem solve using the fundamentals of fatigue and fracture mechanics.
• Utilize ASTM standards to evaluate data sets for valuable material information.
• Create programs to assist with evaluation of large data sets; collecting data on various material properties to further expand the characterization of certain materials.
• Execute analysis on various crack cases to determine critical crack sizes and life expectancies.
• Utilize Internship and hands on experiences to facilitate execution of DT related project tasks leveraging knowledge of structural material property, compatibility, processing, and non-destructive evaluation techniques to develop and provide test data to space flight hardware design teams, design reviews, problem resolution teams, and material usage review teams.
